result.topic_en: Euler continues listing the angles ω that give the vibration frequencies of a free elastic rod, derives the series of simple tones proportional to 25, 81, 169, 289, and notes that the first overtone lies about a comma above a G-sharp relative to a C fundamental.

Corollarium 2.

§. 25. Pergamus igitur ad quartum quadrantem, vbi angulus $\omega$ multo minus discrepabit a $2\pi + 45^\circ$. Hic autem tam finus quam cofinus erit $= +\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$. Simili modo ex feptimo quadrante nancifcimur $\omega = 3\pi + \frac{1}{2}\varrho$, tam finu quam cofinu exiftente $= -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$; nonus vero quadrans fuppeditat $\omega = 4\pi + \frac{1}{2}\varrho$; vndecimus $\omega = 5\pi + \frac{1}{2}\varrho$, et ita porro.

Corollarium 3.

§. 26. Cum igitur fit $\varrho = \frac{\pi}{4}$, omnes valores pro angulo $\omega$ hactenus inuenti fequenti modo progrediuntur:
$1^{dus}\ \omega = \frac{5\pi}{4}$; $2^{dus}\ \omega = \frac{9\pi}{4}$; $3^{us}\ \omega = \frac{13\pi}{4}$; $4^{tus}\ \omega = \frac{17\pi}{4}$, etc.
vnde omnes foni fimplices, quos ifta virga edere poteft, fequentibus numeris exprimentur:
$\frac{25\pi c\sqrt{2gb}}{16aa}$; $\frac{81\pi c\sqrt{2gb}}{16aa}$; $\frac{169\pi c\sqrt{2gb}}{16aa}$; $\frac{289\pi c\sqrt{2gb}}{16aa}$;
quorum primus fundamentalis cenfetur; vnde fi fecundus fimul exaudiatur, erit primus ad fecundum vt 25 ad 81 hoc eft vt $1 : 3\frac{6}{25}$, feu proxime vt $1 : 3\frac{1}{4}$. Ergo fi fonus fundamentalis fuerit C, fequens erit gis, quem tamen fonum vno commate fuperabit, ficque harmonia parum grata exiftet.

Corollarium 4.

§. 27. Cum hic fonus fundamentalis, ceu grauiffimus, quem virga haec edere poteft, fit $= \frac{25\pi c\sqrt{2gb}}{16aa}$, cafu autem

items.quote: Ergo fi fonus fundamentalis fuerit C, fequens erit gis, quem tamen fonum vno commate fuperabit, ficque harmonia parum grata exiftet.
items.english: Therefore if the fundamental tone were C, the following one will be G-sharp, which it will however exceed by one comma, and so the harmony will be hardly pleasing.

items.quote: erit primus ad fecundum vt 25 ad 81 hoc eft vt $1 : 3\frac{6}{25}$, feu proxime vt $1 : 3\frac{1}{4}$
items.english: the first will be to the second as 25 to 81, that is as 1 : 3 6/25, or approximately as 1 : 3 1/4.
